'''''Juncus minutulus''''' is a [[species]] of rush ([[Juncaceae]]) informally<ref name="google">Per Google search, a formal name is unknown</ref> referred to as '''minute rush''', '''dwarf toad rush''' and '''annual rush'''.

==Description==
An annual, resembling and easily confused with a tiny ''[[Juncus bufonius]]'' with all parts smaller and with flowers rarely opening ([[cleistogamous]]): fruit capsule 2.5-3.0mm, [[stamen]]s usually (2)3 instead of 6, anthers 1/4-1/3 x filaments (not 1/3-1 x), [[tepal]]s usually shorter than 4mm, inner tepals acute (not long-tapering), 0-1(2) stem leaves, 1–3cm long.<ref name="SpeciesPlantarum8"/>

''J. bufonius'' also has cleistogamous forms that can very much resemble this in these features therefore all features should be examined carefully (such as inner tepal tip shape).<ref name="holub">[http://old.ibot.cas.cz/preslia/archive/Preslia_48_1976_329-339.pdf Juncus minutulus - přehlížený nový druh československé květeny, 1976, Josef Holub (in Czech and English)]</ref><ref name="Iberica"/>

==Range==
Europe & North Asia, possibly cosmopolitan but reliable records are limited.<ref name="SpeciesPlantarum8">[https://archive.org/details/juncaceae30000unse/mode/2up Species Plantarum / Flora of the World / Part 8. Juncaceae 3: Juncus subg. Agathryon / compiled by Jan Kirschner]</ref><ref name="PoWo">[https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:77084798-1 Plants of the World Online (with map)]</ref>

==Habitat==
Similar to ''[[Juncus bufonius]]'' with which it may grow.

Turkey: Wet or temporarily wet, usually open soil, 0–1800 m.<ref name="FoT9">{{cite book |title=Flora of Turkey and the East Aegean Islands, vol. 9 |author=Davis}}</ref>

Spain: Wet pastures or those in temporarily flooded places, on somewhat saline soils; 0-2900m ("Pastos húmedos o de lugares temporalmente inundados, en suelos algo salinos; 0-2900 m").<ref name="Iberica">[http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/17_172_01_Juncus.pdf Flora iberica (in Spanish)]</ref>

[[Istria]]: Wet roads, fields, ruderal regions.<ref name="Istria">[https://www.researchgate.net/publication/27189168 "The flora of Istria: Juncaceae", 2005, Karl-Georg Bernhardt, Mihaela Britvec]</ref>

Siberia: In wet lowlands, along banks of water reservoirs.<ref name="Siberia">Flora of Siberia vol. 4, 2001 (English Translation)</ref>
